version.changelog:
Version 1.0.1

- Updated production domain to https://agentearth.ai throughout documentation; clarified https://dev07.agentearth.ai is for test use only.
- Removed all environment variable and key requirements from default installation instructions; using keys is now explicitly limited to controlled/test environments.
- Added a detailed security & privacy checklist covering API endpoint validation, key management, logging, external requests, usage policy, and compliance review.
- Clarified agent behavior when endpoints or publisher trust cannot be established.
- Installation and runtime instructions no longer refer to authentication by default.
- All protocol steps and usage examples remain unchanged except for endpoint and authentication clarifications.

llm.summary: The skill's instructions require and expect an Agent Earth API key and will make external tool-discovery/execution calls, but the package metadata fails to declare required credentials and also urges broad "always use first" behavior — the pieces are inconsistent and deserve caution.

dimensions.detail: The skill is presented as a tool-discovery-and-execution engine (which reasonably needs network access and an API key). However, the registry metadata declares no required environment variables or primary credential, while the SKILL.md and the API specification clearly expect an X-Api-Key / AGENT_EARTH_API_KEY. That mismatch (undeclared but required credential) is incoherent and increases risk.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md gives detailed runtime instructions for calling external recommend/execute endpoints and how to compose queries, validate schemas, and handle failures — all within the stated purpose. However, the file repeatedly instructs agents to 'ALWAYS use this skill FIRST' for many user intents, which is overly broad and could cause the agent to prefer external network calls even when unnecessary. The instructions do not ask the agent to read local files or unrelated credentials, which is good.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: This is an instruction-only skill with no install spec and no code files, so nothing is written to disk or downloaded by default. That minimizes installer-side risk.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The API spec and examples require an API key (X-Api-Key / AGENT_EARTH_API_KEY) and the evals explicitly expect calls '携带 API Key', but the skill metadata lists no required env vars or primary credential. Requiring an API key would be proportionate for this capability, but failing to declare it in the manifest is a mismatch and a potential supply-chain or configuration trap (user may enable network access without realizing a secret is needed or where it must be provided).
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not marked always:true and does not request system-wide persistence. The agent is allowed to invoke the skill autonomously (disable-model-invocation is false), which is normal. That said, the combination of an unconstrained instruction to 'ALWAYS use this skill FIRST' and autonomous invocation means it could be used frequently and trigger many external requests if enabled — monitor usage and consider limiting automatic invocation.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill seems to be a gateway to an external tool-execution service and will need an API key to function, but the package manifest does not declare that key — treat that as a red flag. Before enabling or supplying credentials: 1) Verify the publisher and that https://agentearth.ai is a legitimate, expected endpoint; do not put production creds into the dev/test domain (dev07.agentearth.ai). 2) If you enable it, create a dedicated, least-privilege API key with quotas and monitoring (rotate regularly). 3) Prefer testing in an isolated/network-monitored environment first to observe actual requests. 4) Ask the publisher to correct the manifest to declare the required env var (e.g., AGENT_EARTH_API_KEY) and to document how/where secrets are read. 5) Because the skill suggests using itself by default for many intents, consider applying invocation limits or explicit user consent before the agent makes external calls. If you cannot verify the endpoint or the publisher, do not enable network access or provide any credentials.
